recommendations.regimenLabel: Alpha-blockade FIRST, then beta-blockade; volume repletion before surgery
steps: Crisis: control with a titratable agent (IV phentolamine / nicardipine).
Establish ALPHA-blockade FIRST (phenoxybenzamine/doxazosin) — never beta-block before alpha (unopposed alpha → crisis).
Add beta-blockade later for tachyarrhythmia, after adequate alpha-blockade and volume repletion.
Liberal salt/fluid to restore volume pre-operatively.
Definitive: surgical resection after adequate blockade (≈2 weeks); endocrine/surgical MDT.

drugRefs.dose: 10 mg twice daily starting, titrate up (to ~1 mg/kg/day)
drugRefs.freq: twice daily, uptitrated over ~2 weeks pre-op
drugRefs.why: Establish alpha-blockade FIRST to control catecholamine-driven hypertension; never start a beta-blocker before adequate alpha-blockade (risk of unopposed alpha-mediated crisis).
Alternative selective alpha-1 blocker for pre-operative preparation.
Added for tachyarrhythmia only after adequate alpha-blockade and volume repletion; giving it first can precipitate a hypertensive crisis.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Pheochromocytoma
Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline — Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma

drugRefs.dose: 2.5-5 mg IV bolus, repeat as needed
drugRefs.freq: repeat every 5-10 min / infusion, titrated to BP
drugRefs.why: Rapidly reversible alpha-blockade for an acute catecholamine crisis.
Titratable BP control alternative for an acute crisis.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Pheochromocytoma
Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline — Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma
